title: The Coup
one_paragraph_synopsis: In 'The Coup,' the office experiences tension as Dwight seeks to take over management, leading to conflicts with Michael. Dwight accepts the role of acting manager, causing Michael to be demoted. The episode features confrontations, emotional reconciliations, and discussions about leadership and loyalty, culminating in Dwight asserting his leadership and Michael adjusting to his new role.

main_threads.thread: Dwight's attempt to take over management and the subsequent power shift in the office.

evidence.snippet: Jan: No, it wasn't. Dwight just told me that he thinks he can run the branch better than you.
Michael: What was Dwight thinking? That he could turn Jan against me?
Michael: Well, I just got off the phone with Jan. And um… she demoted me.
Michael: And she said that you should be expecting a call later from corporate, and that um, I guess that means that you are going to be acting manager of Dunder Mifflin, Scranton.

Jan (on speakerphone with Michael): Michael.
Michael: Hi.
Jan: I just had a very interesting conversation with one of your employees.
Michael: Oh. That's nice.
Jan: No, it wasn'...
Michael: Hey, hi, hello. Everybody, I have some good news, and I have some bad news. I… am being replaced, as your leader, by Dwight.

character_highlights.what_changes: Dwight accepts the role of acting manager and asserts his leadership.
